title: A finitely presented module free at a prime is free on a principal open neighbourhood
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal and $M$ a finitely presented $A$-module (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus m}\to A^{\oplus n}\to M\to0$ for some $m,n\ge0$; in particular $M$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]). Suppose that the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; since $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is finitely generated it then has a finite basis, of $r$ elements say. Then there is an element $f\in A$, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, such that the localization $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is a finite free $A_f$-module of the same rank: $M_f\cong A_f^{\oplus r}$.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take S = p.primeCompl, f = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M, Rs = Localization.AtPrime p (nontrivial, a local ring), with [Module.FinitePresentation R M] and [Module.Free Rs M_p]; it gives r in S (r not in p) with Module.Free (Localization.Away r) (LocalizedModule.Away r M) and finrank equal to finrank of M_p; M_r is finite over R_r by Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule (RingTheory/Localization/Finiteness.lean:171), so M_r is finite free of rank r. This is exactly how Mathlib's own isOpen_freeLocus (FreeLocus.lean:171-177) uses it. The basis-lifting form is exists_basis_localizedModule_powers (same file, line 41).
